सो ऽन्वपश्यदशेषस्य पार्श्वे तस्य त्रिशूलिनः ।
विशाललोचनमेकां देवीं चारुविलासिनीम् ।
सूर्यायुतसमप्रख्यां प्रसन्नवदनां शिवाम् ॥
2.34.m: He saw at the side of that complete, trident-bearing god / a single large-eyed goddess, gracefully sportive, / resembling ten thousand suns, with a benevolent face, the auspicious Śivā.

2.34.s:
sasmitaṃ prekṣya viśveśaṃ tiṣṭhantīmamitadyutim /
dṛṣṭvā saṃtrastahṛdayo vepamāno munīśvaraḥ /
nanāma śirasā rudraṃ rudrādhyāyaṃ japan vaśī //
2.34.d:
सस्मितं प्रेक्ष्य विश्वेशं तिष्ठन्तीममितद्युतिम् ।
दृष्ट्वा संत्रस्तहृदयो वेपमानो मुनीश्वरः ।
ननाम शिरसा रुद्रं रुद्राध्यायं जपन् वशी ॥
2.34.m: Seeing her standing with an infinite splendor, looking smilingly at the Lord of the universe, / the lord among sages, his heart terrified and trembling, / bowed his head to Rudra, self-controlled and chanting the hymn to Rudra.

2.34.s:
prasanno bhagavānīśastryambako bhaktavatsalaḥ /
pūrvaveṣaṃ sa jagrāha devī cāntarhitābhavat //
2.34.d:
प्रसन्नो भगवानीशस्त्र्यम्बको भक्तवत्सलः ।
पूर्ववेषं स जग्राह देवी चान्तर्हिताभवत् ॥
2.34.m: The blessed Lord Tryambaka, who is affectionate toward his devotees, became pleased; / he assumed his former appearance, and the goddess disappeared.

2.34.s:
āliṅgya bhaktaṃ praṇataṃ devadevaḥ svayaṃśivaḥ /
na bhetavyaṃ tvayā vatsa prāha kiṃ te dadāmyaham //
2.34.d:
आलिङ्ग्य भक्तं प्रणतं देवदेवः स्वयंशिवः ।
न भेतव्यं त्वया वत्स प्राह किं ते ददाम्यहम् ॥
2.34.m: Embracing the bowed devotee, the God of gods, Śiva himself, / said: 'You must not fear, my child; what shall I give to you?'

2.34.s:
praṇamya mūrdhnā giriśaṃ haraṃ tripurasūdanam /
vijñāpayāmāsa tadā hṛṣṭaḥ praṣṭumanā muniḥ //
2.34.d:
प्रणम्य मूर्ध्ना गिरिशं हरं त्रिपुरसूदनम् ।
विज्ञापयामास तदा हृष्टः प्रष्टुमना मुनिः ॥
2.34.m: Bowing with his head to the mountain-dweller, Hara, the destroyer of Tripura, / the delighted sage, wishing to ask, then addressed him:

2.34.s:
namo 'stu te mahādeva maheśvara namo 'stu te /
kimetad bhagavadrūpaṃ sughoraṃ viśvatomukham //
2.34.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते महादेव महेश्वर नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
किमेतद् भगवद्रूपं सुघोरं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
2.34.m: 'Obeisance to you, Mahādeva; obeisance to you, Maheśvara! / What is this form of the Blessed One, so terrifying and facing all directions?

2.34.s:
kā ca sā bhagavatpārśve rājamānā vyavasthitā /
antarhiteva sahasā sarvamicchāmi veditum //
2.34.d:
का च सा भगवत्पार्श्वे राजमाना व्यवस्थिता ।
अन्तर्हितेव सहसा सर्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥
2.34.m: And who was she that stood shining at the side of the Blessed One, / appearing to have vanished all of a sudden? I wish to know everything.'

2.34.s:
ityukte vyājahāramaṃ tathā maṅkaṇakaṃ haraḥ /
maheśaḥ svātmano yogaṃ devīṃ ca tripurānalaḥ //
2.34.d:
इत्युक्ते व्याजहारमं तथा मङ्कणकं हरः ।
महेशः स्वात्मनो योगं देवीं च त्रिपुरानलः ॥
2.34.m: When this was said, Hara, the fire that burned Tripura, / Maheśa, explained to Maṅkaṇaka the yoga of his own Self and the Goddess:

2.34.s:
ahaṃ sahasranayanaḥ sarvātmā sarvatomukhaḥ /
dāhakaḥ sarvapāpānāṃ kālaḥ kālakaro haraḥ //
2.34.d:
अहं सहस्रनयनः सर्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः ।
दाहकः सर्वपापानां कालः कालकरो हरः ॥
2.34.m: 'I am thousand-eyed, the Self of all, facing all directions, / the burner of all sins, Time, the maker of end-time, Hara.

2.34.s:
mayaiva preryate kṛtsnaṃ cetanācetanātmakam /
so 'ntaryāmī sa puruṣo hyahaṃ vai puruṣottamaḥ //
2.34.d:
मयैव प्रेर्यते कृत्स्नं चेतनाचेतनात्मकम् ।
सो ऽन्तर्यामी स पुरुषो ह्यहं वै पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
2.34.m: By me alone is this whole world, composed of the conscious and the unconscious, impelled; / I am that inner ruler, that Spirit, indeed the Supreme Spirit.'

2.34.s:
tasya sā paramā māyā prakṛtistriguṇātmikā /
procyate munirbhiśaktirjagadyoniḥ sanātanī //
2.34.d:
तस्य सा परमा माया प्रकृतिस्त्रिगुणात्मिका ।
प्रोच्यते मुनिर्भिशक्तिर्जगद्योनिः सनातनी ॥
2.34.m:
That supreme illusory creative power of his, primordial matter composed of the three qualities,
is called by the sages the power, the eternal womb of the universe.

2.34.s:
sa eṣa māyayā viśvaṃ vyāmohayati viśvavit /
nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyakto māyārūpa iti śrutiḥ //
2.34.d:
स एष मायया विश्वं व्यामोहयति विश्ववित् ।
नारायणः परो ऽव्यक्तो मायारूप इति श्रुतिः ॥
2.34.m:
He, the knower of all, deludes the universe through his illusory creative power;
revealed scripture states that Nārāyaṇa is the unmanifest supreme, having the form of illusory creative power.

2.34.s:
evametajjagat sarvaṃ sarvadā sthāpayāmyaham /
yojayāmi prakṛtyāhaṃ puruṣaṃ pañcaviṃśakam //
2.34.d:
एवमेतज्जगत् सर्वं सर्वदा स्थापयाम्यहम् ।
योजयामि प्रकृत्याहं पुरुषं पञ्चविंशकम् ॥
2.34.m:
Thus, I always establish this entire universe;
I unite the twenty-fifth principle, the conscious spirit, with primordial matter.

2.34.s:
tathā vai saṃgato devaḥ kūṭasthaḥ sarvago 'malaḥ /
sṛjatyaśeṣamevedaṃ svamūrteḥ prakṛterajaḥ //
2.34.d:
तथा वै संगतो देवः कूटस्थः सर्वगो ऽमलः ।
सृजत्यशेषमेवेदं स्वमूर्तेः प्रकृतेरजः ॥
2.34.m:
Thus indeed united, the God, the immovable, all-pervading, taintless,
unborn one creates this entire world from primordial matter, which is his own form.

2.34.s:
sa devo bhagavān brahmā viśvarūpaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
tavaitat kathitaṃ samyak straṣṭvatvaṃ paramātmanaḥ //
2.34.d:
स देवो भगवान् ब्रह्मा विश्वरूपः पितामहः ।
तवैतत् कथितं सम्यक् स्त्रष्ट्वत्वं परमात्मनः ॥
2.34.m:
He is the Lord God Brahmā, of universal form, the Grandfather;
this nature of the Supreme Self as the creator has been fully told to you.

2.34.s:
eko 'haṃ bhagavān kalo hyanādiścāntakṛd vibhuḥ /
samāsthāya paraṃ bhāvaṃ prokto rudro manīṣibhiḥ //
2.34.d:
एको ऽहं भगवान् कलो ह्यनादिश्चान्तकृद् विभुः ।
समास्थाय परं भावं प्रोक्तो रुद्रो मनीषिभिः ॥
2.34.m:
I alone am the Lord Time, indeed beginningless, bringing about the end, all-pervading;
having assumed the supreme state, I am proclaimed Rudra by the wise.

2.34.s:
mama vai sāparā śaktirdevī vidyeti viśrutā /
dṛṣṭā hi bhavatā nūnaṃ vidyādehastvahaṃ tataḥ //
2.34.d:
मम वै सापरा शक्तिर्देवी विद्येति विश्रुता ।
दृष्टा हि भवता नूनं विद्यादेहस्त्वहं ततः ॥
2.34.m:
Indeed, that other power of mine is the goddess known as Wisdom;
she has certainly been seen by you; therefore I have Wisdom as my body.

2.34.s:
evametāni tattvāni pradhānapuruṣeśvarāḥ /
viṣṇurbrahmā ca bhagavān rudraḥ kāla iti śrutiḥ //
2.34.d:
एवमेतानि तत्त्वानि प्रधानपुरुषेश्वराः ।
विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा च भगवान् रुद्रः काल इति श्रुतिः ॥
2.34.m:
Thus these principles are the primary matter, the conscious spirit, and the Lord;
revealed scripture states that Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and the Lord Rudra are Time.

2.34.s:
trayametadanādyantaṃ brahmaṇyeva vyavasthitam /
tadātmakaṃ tadavyaktaṃ tadakṣaramiti śrutiḥ //
2.34.d:
त्रयमेतदनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्मण्येव व्यवस्थितम् ।
तदात्मकं तदव्यक्तं तदक्षरमिति श्रुतिः ॥
2.34.m:
This triad, without beginning or end, is established in Brahman alone;
revealed scripture states that it is of that nature, that unmanifest, that imperishable.

2.34.s:
ātmānandaparaṃ tattvaṃ cinmātraṃ paramaṃ padam /
ākāśaṃ niṣkalaṃ brahma tasmādanyanna vidyate //
2.34.d:
आत्मानन्दपरं तत्त्वं चिन्मात्रं परमं पदम् ।
आकाशं निष्कलं ब्रह्म तस्मादन्यन्न विद्यते ॥
2.34.m:
The supreme reality is the bliss of the Self, pure consciousness, the highest abode,
ether, the partless Brahman; other than that, nothing exists.

2.34.s:
evaṃ vijñāya bhavatā bhaktiyogāśrayeṇa tu /
saṃpūjyo vandanīyo 'haṃ tatastaṃ paśya śāśvatam //
2.34.d:
एवं विज्ञाय भवता भक्तियोगाश्रयेण तु ।
संपूज्यो वन्दनीयो ऽहं ततस्तं पश्य शाश्वतम् ॥
2.34.m:
Having understood this, by resorting to the yoga of devotion,
I should be worshipped and revered by you; then behold that eternal one.

2.34.s:
etāvaduktvā bhagavāñjagāmādarśanaṃ haraḥ /
tatraiva bhaktiyogena rudrāmārādhayanmuniḥ //
2.34.d:
एतावदुक्त्वा भगवाञ्जगामादर्शनं हरः ।
तत्रैव भक्तियोगेन रुद्रामाराधयन्मुनिः ॥
2.34.m:
Having spoken thus, the Lord Hara disappeared;
right there the sage worshipped Rudra through the yoga of devotion.

2.34.s:
etat pavitramatulaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmarṣisevitam /
saṃsevya brāhmaṇo vidvān mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.34.d:
एतत् पवित्रमतुलं तीर्थं ब्रह्मर्षिसेवितम् ।
संसेव्य ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे चतुस्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.34.m:
Having resorted to this holy, peerless pilgrimage place frequented by Brahmin seers,
a wise Brahmin is freed from all sins.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.35.s:
sūta uvāca
anyat pavitraṃ vipulaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam /
rudrakoṭiriti khyātaṃ rudrasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.35.d:
सूत उवाच
अन्यत् पवित्रं विपुलं तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
रुद्रकोटिरिति ख्यातं रुद्रस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.35.m:
Sūta said:
There is another pure, vast pilgrimage place famous in the three worlds,
known as Rudrakoṭi, belonging to Rudra, the Supreme Being.

2.35.s:
purā puṇyatame kāle devadarśanatatparāḥ /
koṭibrahmarṣayo dāntāstaṃ deśamagaman param //
2.35.d:
पुरा पुण्यतमे काले देवदर्शनतत्पराः ।
कोटिब्रह्मर्षयो दान्तास्तं देशमगमन् परम् ॥
2.35.m:
Long ago, in a most sacred time, intent upon beholding the God,
ten million self-controlled Brahmin seers went to that supreme region.

2.35.s:
ahaṃ drakṣyāmi giriśaṃ pūrvameva pinākinam /
anyo 'nyaṃ bhaktiyuktānāṃ vyāghāto jāyate kila //
2.35.d:
अहं द्रक्ष्यामि गिरिशं पूर्वमेव पिनाकिनम् ।
अन्यो ऽन्यं भक्तियुक्तानां व्याघातो जायते किल ॥
2.35.m:
‘I shall see Giriśa, the bearer of the Pināka, before anyone else!’
Thus an impediment arose mutually among those endowed with devotion.

2.35.s:
teṣāṃ bhaktiṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā giriśo yogināṃ guruḥ /
koṭirūpo 'bhavad rudro rudrakoṭistataḥ smṛtaḥ //
2.35.d:
तेषां भक्तिं तदा दृष्ट्वा गिरिशो योगिनां गुरुः ।
कोटिरूपो ऽभवद् रुद्रो रुद्रकोटिस्ततः स्मृतः ॥
2.35.m:
Beholding their devotion then, Giriśa, the teacher of yogins,
became ten million forms of Rudra; therefore it is remembered as Rudrakoṭi.

2.35.s:
te sma sarve mahādevaṃ haraṃ giriguhāśayam /
paśyantaḥ pārvatīnāthaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭadhiyo 'bhavan //
2.35.d:
ते स्म सर्वे महादेवं हरं गिरिगुहाशयम् ।
पश्यन्तः पार्वतीनाथं हृष्टपुष्टधियो ऽभवन् ॥
2.35.m:
All of them, beholding Mahādeva, Hara, who rests in the mountain cave,
the lord of Pārvatī, became joyful and satisfied in mind.

2.35.s:
anādyantaṃ mahādevaṃ pūrvamevāhamīśvaram /
dṛṣṭavāniti bhaktyā te rudranyastadhiyo 'bhavan //
2.35.d:
अनाद्यन्तं महादेवं पूर्वमेवाहमीश्वरम् ।
दृष्टवानिति भक्त्या ते रुद्रन्यस्तधियो ऽभवन् ॥
2.35.m:
‘I have seen the Lord Mahādeva, without beginning or end, before anyone else!’
Believing thus with devotion, their minds were fixed on Rudra.

2.35.s:
athāntarikṣe vimalaṃ paśyanti sma mahattaram /
jyotistatraiva te sarve 'bhilaṣantaḥ paraṃ padam //
2.35.d:
अथान्तरिक्षे विमलं पश्यन्ति स्म महत्तरम् ।
ज्योतिस्तत्रैव ते सर्वे ऽभिलषन्तः परं पदम् ॥
2.35.m:
Then in the sky they beheld an immaculate, extremely great
radiance right there, desiring the supreme abode.

2.35.s:
etat sadeśādhyuṣitaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyatamaṃ śubham /
dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ samabhyarcya rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt //
2.35.d:
एतत् सदेशाध्युषितं तीर्थं पुण्यतमं शुभम् ।
दृष्ट्वा रुद्रं समभ्यर्च्य रुद्रसामीप्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.35.m:
Having seen and thoroughly worshipped Rudra at this most sacred and auspicious
pilgrimage place inhabited by the virtuous, one attains nearness to Rudra.

2.35.s:
anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ nāmnā madhuvanaṃ smṛtam /
tatra gatvā niyamavānindrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet //
2.35.d:
अन्यच्च तीर्थप्रवरं नाम्ना मधुवनं स्मृतम् ।
तत्र गत्वा नियमवानिन्द्रस्यार्धासनं लभेत् ॥
2.35.m:
And there is another excellent pilgrimage place, remembered by the name Madhuvana;
having gone there, disciplined by vows, one obtains half of Indra's seat.

2.35.s:
athānyatpuṣpanagarī deśaḥ puṇyatamaḥ śubhaḥ /
tatra gatvā pitṝn pūjya kulānāṃ tārayecchatam //
2.35.d:
अथान्यत्पुष्पनगरी देशः पुण्यतमः शुभः ।
तत्र गत्वा पितॄन् पूज्य कुलानां तारयेच्छतम् ॥
2.35.m:
Then there is another, Puṣpanagarī, a most sacred and auspicious region;
having gone there and worshipped the ancestors, one delivers a hundred families across.

2.35.s:
kālañjaraṃ mahātīrthaṃ loke rudro maheśvaraḥ /
kālaṃ jaritavān devo yatra bhaktipriyo haraḥ //
2.35.d:
कालञ्जरं महातीर्थं लोके रुद्रो महेश्वरः ।
कालं जरितवान् देवो यत्र भक्तिप्रियो हरः ॥
2.35.m:
Kālañjara is a great pilgrimage place where Rudra Maheśvara, the God,
Hara who is fond of devotion, caused Time (Kāla) to age in this world.

2.35.s:
śveto nāma śive bhakto rājarṣipravaraḥ purā /
tadāśīstannamaskāraḥ pūjayāmāsa śūlinam //
2.35.d:
श्वेतो नाम शिवे भक्तो राजर्षिप्रवरः पुरा ।
तदाशीस्तन्नमस्कारः पूजयामास शूलिनम् ॥
2.35.m:
Long ago, an eminent royal seer named Śveta was devoted to Śiva;
offering his blessings and obeisances to him, he worshipped the bearer of the trident.

2.35.s:
saṃsthāpya vidhinā liṅgaṃ bhaktiyogapuraḥ saraḥ /
jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ tatra saṃnyastamānasaḥ //
2.35.d:
संस्थाप्य विधिना लिङ्गं भक्तियोगपुरः सरः ।
जजाप रुद्रमनिशं तत्र संन्यस्तमानसः ॥
2.35.m:
Having installed a liṅga according to rule, preceded by the yoga of devotion,
with his mind surrendered unto it, he chanted Rudra's [hymn] day and night.

2.35.s:
sa taṃ kālo 'tha dīptātmā śūlamādāya bhīṣaṇam /
netumabhyāgato deśaṃ sa rājā yatra tiṣṭhati //
2.35.d:
स तं कालो ऽथ दीप्तात्मा शूलमादाय भीषणम् ।
नेतुमभ्यागतो देशं स राजा यत्र तिष्ठति ॥
2.35.m:
Then Time of blazing self, seizing a terrifying trident,
arrived to carry him away to that place where the king stood.

2.35.s:
vīkṣya rājā bhayāviṣṭaḥ śūlahastaṃ samāgatam /
kālaṃ kālakaraṃ ghoraṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ caṇḍadīdhitim //
2.35.d:
वीक्ष्य राजा भयाविष्टः शूलहस्तं समागतम् ।
कालं कालकरं घोरं भीषणं चण्डदीधितिम् ॥
2.35.m:
Seeing that terrible, fierce, frightful Time of scorching splendor,
who brings death, arrive with trident in hand, the king was overcome with fear.

2.35.s:
ubābhyāmatha hastābhyāṃ spṛṭvāsau liṅgamaiśvaram /
nanāma śirasā rudraṃ jajāpa śatarudriyam //
2.35.d:
उबाभ्यामथ हस्ताभ्यां स्पृट्वासौ लिङ्गमैश्वरम् ।
ननाम शिरसा रुद्रं जजाप शतरुद्रियम् ॥
2.35.m:
Then, touching the divine liṅga with both hands,
he bowed his head to Rudra and chanted the Śatarudriya.

2.35.s:
japantamāha rājānaṃ namantamasakṛd bhavam /
ehyehīti puraḥ sthitvā kṛtāntaḥ prahasanniva //
2.35.d:
जपन्तमाह राजानं नमन्तमसकृद् भवम् ।
एह्येहीति पुरः स्थित्वा कृतान्तः प्रहसन्निव ॥
2.35.m:
Standing in front of the chanting king who repeatedly bowed to Bhava,
Death spoke to him as if laughing: ‘Come, come!’

2.35.s:
tamuvāca bhayāviṣṭo rājā rudraparāyaṇaḥ /
ekamīśārcanarataṃ vihāyānyaṃ niṣūdaya //
2.35.d:
तमुवाच भयाविष्टो राजा रुद्रपरायणः ।
एकमीशार्चनरतं विहायान्यं निषूदय ॥
2.35.m:
Overcome with fear, the king, intent upon Rudra, said to him:
‘Leaving this one devoted to the worship of the Lord, slay another!’

2.35.s:
ityuktavantaṃ bhagavānabravīd bhītamānasam /
rudrārcanarato vānyo madvaśe ko na tiṣṭhati //
2.35.d:
इत्युक्तवन्तं भगवानब्रवीद् भीतमानसम् ।
रुद्रार्चनरतो वान्यो मद्वशे को न तिष्ठति ॥
2.35.m:
To him who had spoken thus, the Lord [Time] said to his frightened mind:
‘Whether devoted to the worship of Rudra or another, who does not stay under my control?’

2.35.s:
evamuktvā sa rājānaṃ kālo lokaprakālanaḥ /
babandha pāśai rājāpi jajāpa śatarudriyam //
2.35.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स राजानं कालो लोकप्रकालनः ।
बबन्ध पाशै राजापि जजाप शतरुद्रियम् ॥
2.35.m:
Having spoken thus to the king, Time, who drives forth the worlds,
bound [him] with nooses, yet the king still chanted the Śatarudriya.

2.35.s:
athāntarikṣe vimalaṃ dīpyamānaṃ
tejorāśiṃ bhūtabhartuḥ purāṇam /
jvālāmālāsaṃvṛtaṃ vyāpya viśvaṃ
prādurbhūtaṃ saṃsthitaṃ saṃdadarśa //
2.35.d:
अथान्तरिक्षे विमलं दीप्यमानं
तेजोराशिं भूतभर्तुः पुराणम् ।
ज्वालामालासंवृतं व्याप्य विश्वं
प्रादुर्भूतं संस्थितं संददर्श ॥
2.35.m:
Then in the sky he beheld the ancient mass of splendor
of the Lord of beings, spotless and blazing,
surrounded by garlands of flames, pervading the universe,
manifested and stationed [there].

2.35.s:
tanmadhye 'sau puruṣaṃ rukmavarṇaṃ
devyā devaṃ candralekhojjvalāṅgam /
tejorūpaṃ paśyati smātihṛṣṭo
mene cāsmannātha āgacchatīti //
2.35.d:
तन्मध्ये ऽसौ पुरुषं रुक्मवर्णं
देव्या देवं चन्द्रलेखोज्ज्वलाङ्गम् ।
तेजोरूपं पश्यति स्मातिहृष्टो
मेने चास्मन्नाथ आगच्छतीति ॥
2.35.m:
In its midst he saw the Person of golden hue,
the God with the Goddess, his limbs shining with the crescent moon,
embodied as radiance; highly delighted, he thought: ‘Our Lord has come!’

2.35.s:
āgacchantaṃ nātidūre 'tha dṛṣṭvā
kālo rudraṃ devadevyā maheśam /
vyapetabhīrakhileśaikanāthaṃ
rājarṣistaṃ netumabhyājagāma //
2.35.d:
आगच्छन्तं नातिदूरे ऽथ दृष्ट्वा
कालो रुद्रं देवदेव्या महेशम् ।
व्यपेतभीरखिलेशैकनाथं
राजर्षिस्तं नेतुमभ्याजगाम ॥

2.35.s:
ālokyāsau bhagavānugrakarmā
devo rudro bhūtabhartā purāṇaḥ /
ekaṃ bhaktaṃ matparaṃ māṃ smarantaṃ
dehītīmaṃ kālamūce mameti //
2.35.d:
आलोक्यासौ भगवानुग्रकर्मा
देवो रुद्रो भूतभर्ता पुराणः ।
एकं भक्तं मत्परं मां स्मरन्तं
देहीतीमं कालमूचे ममेति ॥
2.35.m:
Beholding this, that Lord of fierce deeds,
the God Rudra, the ancient Lord of beings,
said to Time: ‘Give [me] this single devotee who is devoted to me, remembering me as mine!’

2.35.s:
śrutvā vākhyaṃ gopaterugrabhāvaḥ
kālātmāsau manyamānaḥ svabhāvam /
baddhvā bhaktaṃ punarevātha pāśaiḥ
kruddho rudramabhidudrāva vegāt //
2.35.d:
श्रुत्वा वाख्यं गोपतेरुग्रभावः
कालात्मासौ मन्यमानः स्वभावम् ।
बद्ध्वा भक्तं पुनरेवाथ पाशैः
क्रुद्धो रुद्रमभिदुद्राव वेगात् ॥
2.35.m:
Hearing the words of the Lord of herds, he of ferocious nature,
whose nature is Time, asserting his own essence,
having bound the devotee again with nooses,
rushed furiously toward Rudra with speed.

2.35.s:
prekṣyāyāntaṃ śailaputrīmatheśaḥ
so 'nvīkṣyānte viśvamāyāvidhijñaḥ /
sāvajñaṃ vai vāmapādena mṛtyuṃ
śvetasyainaṃ paśyato vyājaghāna //
2.35.d:
प्रेक्ष्यायान्तं शैलपुत्रीमथेशः
सो ऽन्वीक्ष्यान्ते विश्वमायाविधिज्ञः ।
सावज्ञं वै वामपादेन मृत्युं
श्वेतस्यैनं पश्यतो व्याजघान ॥
2.35.m: Then the Lord, who knows the working of all cosmic illusion, / seeing the Daughter of the Mountain and looking at the end, / contemptuously struck Death with his left foot / while Śveta looked on.

2.35.s:
mamāra so 'tibhīṣaṇo maheśapādaghātitaḥ /
rarāja devatāpatiḥ sahomayā pinākadhṛk //
2.35.d:
ममार सो ऽतिभीषणो महेशपादघातितः ।
रराज देवतापतिः सहोमया पिनाकधृक् ॥
2.35.m: That most terrifying one, struck down by Maheśvara's foot, died; / and the Lord of deities, holder of the Pināka bow, shone forth along with Umā.

2.35.s:
nirīkṣya devamīśvaraṃ prahṛṣṭamānaso haram /
nanāma sāmbamavyayaṃ sa rājapuṅgavastadā //
2.35.d:
निरीक्ष्य देवमीश्वरं प्रहृष्टमानसो हरम् ।
ननाम साम्बमव्ययं स राजपुङ्गवस्तदा ॥
2.35.m: Beholding the Lord, the deity Hara, with joyful mind, / that eminent king then bowed to the imperishable Lord with Ambā:

2.35.s:
namo bhavāya hetave harāya viśvasaṃbhave /
namaḥ śivāya dhīmate namo 'pavargadāyine //
2.35.d:
नमो भवाय हेतवे हराय विश्वसंभवे ।
नमः शिवाय धीमते नमो ऽपवर्गदायिने ॥
2.35.m: "Salutations to Bhava, to the Cause, to Hara, the origin of the universe! / Salutations to Śiva the wise, salutations to the bestower of liberation!

2.35.s:
namo namo namo 'stu te mahāvibhūtaye namaḥ /
vibhāgahīnarūpiṇe namo narādhipāya te //
2.35.d:
नमो नमो नमो ऽस्तु ते महाविभूतये नमः ।
विभागहीनरूपिणे नमो नराधिपाय ते ॥
2.35.m: Salutations, salutations, salutations be to you! Salutations to the one of great sovereign glory! / To the one whose form is indivisible, salutations to you, the sovereign ruler of men!

2.35.s:
namo 'stu te gaṇeśvara prapannaduḥ khanāśana /
anādinityabhūtaye varāhaśṛṅgadhāriṇe //
2.35.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते गणेश्वर प्रपन्नदुः खनाशन ।
अनादिनित्यभूतये वराहशृङ्गधारिणे ॥
2.35.m: Salutations be to you, Lord of the retinue, destroyer of the suffering of the surrendered! / To the one of beginningless and eternal sovereign glory, to the wearer of the boar's tusk!

2.35.s:
namo vṛṣadhvajāya te kapālamāline namaḥ /
namo mahānaṭāya te namo vṛṣadhvajāya te //
2.35.d:
नमो वृषध्वजाय ते कपालमालिने नमः ।
नमो महानटाय ते नमो वृषध्वजाय ते ॥
2.35.m: Salutations to you whose banner is the bull, salutations to the wearer of the garland of skulls! / Salutations to you, the great dancer! Salutations to you whose banner is the bull!"

2.35.s:
athānugṛhya śaṅkaraḥ praṇāmatatparaṃ nṛpam /
svagāṇapatyamavyayaṃ sarūpatāmatho dadau //
2.35.d:
अथानुगृह्य शङ्करः प्रणामतत्परं नृपम् ।
स्वगाणपत्यमव्ययं सरूपतामथो ददौ ॥
2.35.m: Then, having shown grace to the king devoted to bowing, Śaṅkara / bestowed his own imperishable leadership of the retinue and similarity of divine form.

2.35.s:
sahomayā sapārṣadaḥ sarājapuṅgavo haraḥ /
munīśasiddhavanditaḥ kṣaṇādadṛśyatāmagāt //
2.35.d:
सहोमया सपार्षदः सराजपुङ्गवो हरः ।
मुनीशसिद्धवन्दितः क्षणाददृश्यतामगात् ॥
2.35.m: Hara, accompanied by Umā, his attendants, and the eminent king, / praised by eminent sages and Siddhas, vanished in an instant.

2.35.s:
kāle maheśābhihate lokanāthaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
ayācata varaṃ rudraṃ sajīvo 'yaṃ bhavatviti //
2.35.d:
काले महेशाभिहते लोकनाथः पितामहः ।
अयाचत वरं रुद्रं सजीवो ऽयं भवत्विति ॥
2.35.m: When Death had been struck down by Maheśvara, the grandfather, the Lord of the worlds, / asked a boon of Rudra: "Let him become alive again!

2.35.s:
nāsti kaścidapīśāna doṣaleśo vṛṣadhvaja /
kṛtāntasyaiva bhavatā tatkārye viniyojitaḥ //
2.35.d:
नास्ति कश्चिदपीशान दोषलेशो वृषध्वज ।
कृतान्तस्यैव भवता तत्कार्ये विनियोजितः ॥
2.35.m: There is not the least fault, O Īśāna, O you whose banner is the bull, / on the part of Death; he was merely appointed by you to that task."

2.35.s:
sa devadevavacanād devadeveśvaro haraḥ /
tathāstvityāha viśvātmā so 'pi tādṛgvidho 'bhavat //
2.35.d:
स देवदेववचनाद् देवदेवेश्वरो हरः ।
तथास्त्वित्याह विश्वात्मा सो ऽपि तादृग्विधो ऽभवत् ॥
2.35.m: At the words of the god of gods, Hara, the sovereign Lord of the gods of gods and Soul of all, / said, "So be it"; and he too became as he had been.

2.35.s:
ityetat paramaṃ tīrthaṃ kālañjaramiti śrutam /
gatvābhyarcya mahādevaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ sa vindati //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.35.d:
इत्येतत् परमं तीर्थं कालञ्जरमिति श्रुतम् ।
गत्वाभ्यर्च्य महादेवं गाणपत्यं स विन्दति ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे पञ्चत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.35.m:
Thus this is the supreme sacred ford renowned as Kālañjara. / Having gone and worshipped Mahādeva there, one attains leadership of his retinue.

Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.36.s:
sūta uvāca
idanamanyate paraṃ sthānaṃ guhyād guhyatamaṃ mahat /
mahādevasya devasya mahālayamiti śrutam //
2.36.d:
सूत उवाच
इदनमन्यते परं स्थानं गुह्याद् गुह्यतमं महत् ।
महादेवस्य देवस्य महालयमिति श्रुतम् ॥
2.36.m: Sūta said: / Now another supreme place is considered, most secret of secrets, great, / renowned as Mahālaya, belonging to the deity Mahādeva.

2.36.s:
tatra devādidevena rudreṇa tripurāriṇā /
śilātale padaṃ nyastaṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam //
2.36.d:
तत्र देवादिदेवेन रुद्रेण त्रिपुरारिणा ।
शिलातले पदं न्यस्तं नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् ॥
2.36.m: There, the first god of gods, Rudra, the enemy of Tripura, / placed his footprint upon a slab of rock as evidence for atheists.

2.36.s:
tatra puśupatāḥ śāntā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ /
upāsate mahādevaṃ vedādhyayanatatparāḥ //
2.36.d:
तत्र पुशुपताः शान्ता भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहाः ।
उपासते महादेवं वेदाध्ययनतत्पराः ॥
2.36.m: There tranquil Pāśupatas, their bodies smeared with ash, / devoted to Vedic study, worship Mahādeva.

2.36.s:
snātvā tatra padaṃ śārvaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktipuraḥ saram /
namaskṛtvātha śirasā rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt //
2.36.d:
स्नात्वा तत्र पदं शार्वं दृष्ट्वा भक्तिपुरः सरम् ।
नमस्कृत्वाथ शिरसा रुद्रसामीप्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.36.m: Having bathed there, beholding the footprint of Śarva with devotion, / and bowing with one's head, one attains proximity to Rudra.

2.36.s:
anyacca devadevasya sthānaṃ śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ /
kedāramiti vikhyātaṃ siddhānāmālayaṃ śubham //
2.36.d:
अन्यच्च देवदेवस्य स्थानं शंभोर्महात्मनः ।
केदारमिति विख्यातं सिद्धानामालयं शुभम् ॥
2.36.m: There is also another auspicious dwelling of the Siddhas, a place of the great-souled Śambhu, / the god of gods, celebrated as Kedāra.

2.36.s:
tatra snātvā mahādevamabhyarcya vṛṣaketanam /
pītvā caivodakaṃ śuddhaṃ gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt //
2.36.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा महादेवमभ्यर्च्य वृषकेतनम् ।
पीत्वा चैवोदकं शुद्धं गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.36.m: Having bathed there, worshipped Mahādeva whose banner is the bull, / and drunk pure water, one attains leadership of his retinue.

2.36.s:
śrāddhadānādikaṃ kṛtvā hyakṣyaṃ labhate phalam /
dvijātipravarairjuṣṭaṃ yogibhiryatamānasaiḥ //
2.36.d:
श्राद्धदानादिकं कृत्वा ह्यक्ष्यं लभते फलम् ।
द्विजातिप्रवरैर्जुष्टं योगिभिर्यतमानसैः ॥
2.36.m: Performing ancestral offering rites, gifts, and the like, one obtains an imperishable fruit. / It is frequented by eminent twice-born people and by yogins with restrained minds.

2.36.s:
tīrthaṃ plakṣāvataraṇaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam /
tatrābhyarcya śrīnivāsaṃ viṣṇuloke mahīyate //
2.36.d:
तीर्थं प्लक्षावतरणं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ।
तत्राभ्यर्च्य श्रीनिवासं विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥
2.36.m: The sacred ford Plakṣāvataraṇa destroys all sins; / having worshipped the Abode of Śrī there, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

2.36.s:
anyaṃ magadharājasya tīrthaṃ svargagatipradam /
akṣayaṃ vindati svargaṃ tatra gatvā dvijottamaḥ //
2.36.d:
अन्यं मगधराजस्य तीर्थं स्वर्गगतिप्रदम् ।
अक्षयं विन्दति स्वर्गं तत्र गत्वा द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.36.m: There is another sacred ford belonging to the king of Magadha that grants the course to heaven; / having gone there, an excellent twice-born person attains imperishable heaven.

2.36.s:
tīrthaṃ kanakhalaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam /
yatra devena rudreṇa yajño dakṣasya nāśitaḥ //
2.36.d:
तीर्थं कनखलं पुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् ।
यत्र देवेन रुद्रेण यज्ञो दक्षस्य नाशितः ॥
2.36.m: The holy sacred ford Kanakhala destroys great sins, / where the sacrifice of Dakṣa was destroyed by the god Rudra.

2.36.s:
tatra gaṅgāmupaspṛśya śucirbhāvasamanvitaḥ /
mucyate sarvapāpaistu brahmalokaṃ labhenmṛtaḥ //
2.36.d:
तत्र गङ्गामुपस्पृश्य शुचिर्भावसमन्वितः ।
मुच्यते सर्वपापैस्तु ब्रह्मलोकं लभेन्मृतः ॥
2.36.m: Having touched the Gaṅgā there, pure and endowed with faith, / one is freed from all sins, and upon dying attains the world of Brahmā.

2.36.s:
mahātīrthamiti khyātaṃ puṇyaṃ nārāyaṇapriyam /
tatrābhyarcya hṛṣīkeśaṃ śvetadvīpaṃ nigacchati //
2.36.d:
महातीर्थमिति ख्यातं पुण्यं नारायणप्रियम् ।
तत्राभ्यर्च्य हृषीकेशं श्वेतद्वीपं निगच्छति ॥
2.36.m: The sacred ford renowned as Mahātīrtha is holy and dear to Nārāyaṇa; / having worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa there, one goes to Śvetadvīpa.

2.36.s:
anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ nāmnā śrīparvataṃ śubham /
tatra prāṇān parityajya rudrasya dayito bhavet //
2.36.d:
अन्यच्च तीर्थप्रवरं नाम्ना श्रीपर्वतं शुभम् ।
तत्र प्राणान् परित्यज्य रुद्रस्य दयितो भवेत् ॥
2.36.m: There is also an auspicious, excellent sacred ford named Śrīparvata; / having abandoned one's life-breaths there, one becomes beloved of Rudra.

2.36.s:
tatra sannihito rudro devyā saha maheśvaraḥ /
snānapiṇḍādikaṃ tatra kṛtamakṣayyamuttamam //
2.36.d:
तत्र सन्निहितो रुद्रो देव्या सह महेश्वरः ।
स्नानपिण्डादिकं तत्र कृतमक्षय्यमुत्तमम् ॥
2.36.m: There Maheśvara Rudra is ever present along with the goddess; / bathing, offering funeral balls, and the like done there become imperishable and supreme.

2.36.s:
godāvarī nadī puṇyā sarvapāpavināśanī /
tatra snātvā pitṝn devāṃstarpayitvā yathāvidhi /
sarvapāpavisuddhātmā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet //
2.36.d:
गोदावरी नदी पुण्या सर्वपापविनाशनी ।
तत्र स्नात्वा पितॄन् देवांस्तर्पयित्वा यथाविधि ।
सर्वपापविसुद्धात्मा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥
2.36.m: The holy river Godāvarī destroys all sins; / having bathed there and gratified the ancestors and gods according to the rules, / purified of all sins, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.

2.36.s:
pavitrasalilā puṇyā kāverī vipulā nadī /
tasyāṃ snātvodakaṃ kṛtvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ /
trirātropoṣitenātha ekarātroṣitena vā //
2.36.d:
पवित्रसलिला पुण्या कावेरी विपुला नदी ।
तस्यां स्नात्वोदकं कृत्वा मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ।
त्रिरात्रोपोषितेनाथ एकरात्रोषितेन वा ॥
2.36.m: The vast river Kāverī is holy, with pure waters; / having bathed and offered water in it after fasting for three nights or one night, / one is freed from all sins.

2.36.s:
dvijātīnāṃ tu kathitaṃ tīrthānāmiha sevanam /
yasya vāṅmanaso śuddhe hastapādau ca saṃsthitau /
alolupo brahmacāro tīrthānāṃ phalamāpnuyāt //
2.36.d:
द्विजातीनां तु कथितं तीर्थानामिह सेवनम् ।
यस्य वाङ्मनसो शुद्धे हस्तपादौ च संस्थितौ ।
अलोलुपो ब्रह्मचारो तीर्थानां फलमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.36.m: This resort to sacred fords has been prescribed for the twice-born: / he whose speech and mind are pure, whose hands and feet are restrained, / who is free from greed and observes celibacy, obtains the fruit of sacred fords.

2.36.s:
svāmitīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam /
tatra sannihito nityaṃ skando 'maranamaskṛtaḥ //
2.36.d:
स्वामितीर्थं महातीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ।
तत्र सन्निहितो नित्यं स्कन्दो ऽमरनमस्कृतः ॥
2.36.m: Svāmitīrtha is a great sacred ford renowned in the three worlds; / Skanda, bowed to by the immortals, is ever present there.

2.36.s:
snātvā kumāradhārāyāṃ kṛtvā devāditarpaṇam /
ārādhya ṣaṇmukhaṃ devaṃ skandena saha modate //
2.36.d:
स्नात्वा कुमारधारायां कृत्वा देवादितर्पणम् ।
आराध्य षण्मुखं देवं स्कन्देन सह मोदते ॥
2.36.m: Having bathed in Kumāradhārā and performed the gratifications to gods and others, / and having worshipped the six-faced deity, one rejoices with Skanda.

2.36.s:
nadī trailokyavikhyātā tāmraparṇoti nāmataḥ /
tatra snātvā pitṝn bhaktyā tarpayitvā yathāvidhi /
pāpakartṝnapi pitṝstārayennātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.36.d:
नदी त्रैलोक्यविख्याता ताम्रपर्णोति नामतः ।
तत्र स्नात्वा पितॄन् भक्त्या तर्पयित्वा यथाविधि ।
पापकर्तॄनपि पितॄस्तारयेन्नात्र संशयः ॥
2.36.m: There is a river renowned across the three worlds by the name Tāmraparṇī; / having bathed there and gratified the ancestors with devotion according to the rules, / one delivers even sin-committing ancestors—of this there is no doubt.

2.36.s:
candratīrthamiti khyātaṃ kāveryāḥ prabhave 'kṣayam /
tīrthaṃ tatra bhaved vastuṃ mṛtānāṃ svargatirdhruvā //
2.36.d:
चन्द्रतीर्थमिति ख्यातं कावेर्याः प्रभवे ऽक्षयम् ।
तीर्थं तत्र भवेद् वस्तुं मृतानां स्वर्गतिर्ध्रुवा ॥
2.36.m: The imperishable sacred ford known as Candratīrtha is at the source of the Kāverī; / to dwell at that sacred ford ensures heaven for those who die there.

2.36.s:
vindhyapāde prapaśyanti devadevaṃ sadāśivam /
bhaktyā ye te na paśyanti yamasya sadanaṃ dvijāḥ //
2.36.d:
विन्ध्यपादे प्रपश्यन्ति देवदेवं सदाशिवम् ।
भक्त्या ये ते न पश्यन्ति यमस्य सदनं द्विजाः ॥
2.36.m: Those who with devotion behold the god of gods, Sadāśiva, at the foot of the Vindhya, / do not see the abode of Yama, O twice-born ones.

2.36.s:
devikāyāṃ vṛṣo nāma tīrthaṃ siddhaniṣevitam /
tatra snātvodakaṃ datvā yogasiddhiṃ ca vindati //
2.36.d:
देविकायां वृषो नाम तीर्थं सिद्धनिषेवितम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वोदकं दत्वा योगसिद्धिं च विन्दति ॥
2.36.m: On the Devikā is a sacred ford named Vṛṣa, frequented by Siddhas; / having bathed there and offered water, one attains success in yoga.

2.36.s:
daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam /
daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ tatrāpnoti phalaṃ naraḥ //
2.36.d:
दशाश्वमेधिकं तीर्थं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ।
दशानामश्वमेधानां तत्राप्नोति फलं नरः ॥
2.36.m: The sacred ford Daśāśvamedhika destroys all sins; / a man attains there the fruit of ten horse sacrifices.

2.36.s:
puṇḍarīkaṃ mahātīrthaṃ brāhmaṇairupasevitam /
tatrābhigamya yuktātmā pauṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet //
2.36.d:
पुण्डरीकं महातीर्थं ब्राह्मणैरुपसेवितम् ।
तत्राभिगम्य युक्तात्मा पौण्डरीकफलं लभेत् ॥
2.36.m: The great sacred ford Puṇḍarīka is frequented by brāhmaṇas; / having gone there with concentrated mind, one obtains the fruit of a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.

2.36.s:
tīrthebhyaḥ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmatīrthamiti śrutam /
brahmāṇamarcayitvā tu brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.36.d:
तीर्थेभ्यः परमं तीर्थं ब्रह्मतीर्थमिति श्रुतम् ।
ब्रह्माणमर्चयित्वा तु ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.36.m: The sacred ford supreme among sacred fords is renowned as Brahmatīrtha; / having worshipped Brahmā there, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

2.36.s:
sarasvatyā vinaśanaṃ plakṣaprastravaṇaṃ śubham /
vyāsatīrthaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ mainākaṃ ca nagottamam /
yamunāprabhavaṃ caiva sarvapāpaviśodhanam //
2.36.d:
सरस्वत्या विनशनं प्लक्षप्रस्त्रवणं शुभम् ।
व्यासतीर्थं परं तीर्थं मैनाकं च नगोत्तमम् ।
यमुनाप्रभवं चैव सर्वपापविशोधनम् ॥
2.36.m: The disappearance of the Sarasvatī, the auspicious Plakṣaprastravaṇa, / the supreme Vyāsatīrtha, Maināka the best of mountains, / and the source of the Yamunā purify all sins.

2.36.s:
pitṝṇāṃ duhitā devī gandhakālīti viśrutā /
tasyāṃ snātvā divaṃ yāti mṛto jātismaro bhavet //
2.36.d:
पितॄणां दुहिता देवी गन्धकालीति विश्रुता ।
तस्यां स्नात्वा दिवं याति मृतो जातिस्मरो भवेत् ॥
2.36.m: The goddess celebrated as Gandhakālī is the daughter of the ancestors; / having bathed in her, one goes to heaven, and when dead, remembers one's former births.

2.36.s:
kuberatuṅgaṃ pāpaghnaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam /
prāṇāṃstatra parityajya kuberānucaro bhavet //
2.36.d:
कुबेरतुङ्गं पापघ्नं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ।
प्राणांस्तत्र परित्यज्य कुबेरानुचरो भवेत् ॥
2.36.m: Kuberatuṅga destroys sin and is frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas; / having abandoned one's life-breaths there, one becomes an attendant of Kubera.

2.36.s:
umātuṅgamiti khyātaṃ yatra sā rudravallabhā /
tatrābhyarcya mahādevīṃ kosahasraphalaṃ labhet //
2.36.d:
उमातुङ्गमिति ख्यातं यत्र सा रुद्रवल्लभा ।
तत्राभ्यर्च्य महादेवीं कोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥
2.36.m: The peak known as Umātuṅga is where that beloved of Rudra dwells; / having worshipped the Great Goddess there, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.

2.36.s:
bhṛgutuṅge tapastaptaṃ śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tathā kṛtam /
kulānyubhayataḥ sapta punātīti śrutirmama //
2.36.d:
भृगुतुङ्गे तपस्तप्तं श्राद्धं दानं तथा कृतम् ।
कुलान्युभयतः सप्त पुनातीति श्रुतिर्मम ॥
2.36.m: Austerity performed, ancestral offering rites, and gifts made on Bhṛgutuṅga / purify seven generations on both sides—such is my scriptural tradition.

2.36.s:
kāśyapasya mahātīrthaṃ kālasarpiriti śrutam /
tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityaṃ pāpakṣayecchayā //
2.36.d:
काश्यपस्य महातीर्थं कालसर्पिरिति श्रुतम् ।
तत्र श्राद्धानि देयानि नित्यं पापक्षयेच्छया ॥
2.36.m: The great holy place of Kaśyapa is known as Kālasarpi. / There ancestral offering rites should always be performed by one desiring the destruction of sins.

2.36.s:
daśārṇāyāṃ tathā dānaṃ śrāddhaṃ homastathā japaḥ /
akṣayaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva kṛtaṃ bhavati sarvadā //
2.36.d:
दशार्णायां तथा दानं श्राद्धं होमस्तथा जपः ।
अक्षयं चाव्ययं चैव कृतं भवति सर्वदा ॥
2.36.m: Likewise, a gift, an ancestral offering rite, a fire oblation, and muttering [of mantras] at Daśārṇā, / once performed, always becomes imperishable and inexhaustible.

2.36.s:
tīrthaṃ dvijātibhirjuṣṭaṃ nāmnā vai kurujāṅgalam /
dattvā tu dānaṃ vidhivad brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.36.d:
तीर्थं द्विजातिभिर्जुष्टं नाम्ना वै कुरुजाङ्गलम् ।
दत्त्वा तु दानं विधिवद् ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.36.m: There is a holy place frequented by twice-born men, indeed named Kurujāṅgala; / having given a gift there according to rule, one is exalted in the realm of Brahmā.

2.36.s:
vaitaraṇyāṃ mahātīrthe svarṇavedyāṃ tathaiva ca /
dharmapṛṣṭhe ca sarasi brahmaṇaḥ parame śubhe //
2.36.d:
वैतरण्यां महातीर्थे स्वर्णवेद्यां तथैव च ।
धर्मपृष्ठे च सरसि ब्रह्मणः परमे शुभे ॥
2.36.m: At the great holy place Vaitaraṇī, and likewise at Svarṇavedī, / and at Dharmapṛṣṭha, at the supremely auspicious lake of Brahmā,

2.36.s:
bharatasyāśrame puṇye puṇye śrāddhavaṭe śubhe /
mahāhrade ca kauśikyāṃ dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam //
2.36.d:
भरतस्याश्रमे पुण्ये पुण्ये श्राद्धवटे शुभे ।
महाह्रदे च कौशिक्यां दत्तं भवति चाक्षयम् ॥
2.36.m: at the holy hermitage of Bharata, at the holy, auspicious Śrāddhavaṭa, / and at the great pool at Kauśikī, what is given becomes imperishable.

2.36.s:
muñjapṛṣṭhe padaṃ nyastaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā /
hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam //
2.36.d:
मुञ्जपृष्ठे पदं न्यस्तं महादेवेन धीमता ।
हिताय सर्वभूतानां नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् ॥
2.36.m: On Muñjapṛṣṭha a footprint was placed by wise Mahādeva / for the benefit of all beings, as a demonstration to atheists.

2.36.s:
alpenāpi tu kālena naro dharmaparāyaṇaḥ /
pāpmānamutsṛjatyāśu jīrṇāṃ tvacamivoragaḥ //
2.36.d:
अल्पेनापि तु कालेन नरो धर्मपरायणः ।
पाप्मानमुत्सृजत्याशु जीर्णां त्वचमिवोरगः ॥
2.36.m: Even in a short time, a person devoted to righteousness / quickly casts off sin, like a snake its worn-out skin.

2.36.s:
nāmnā kanakanandeti tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam /
udīcyāṃ muñjapṛṣṭhasya brahmarṣigaṇasevitam //
2.36.d:
नाम्ना कनकनन्देति तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
उदीच्यां मुञ्जपृष्ठस्य ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम् ॥
2.36.m: To the north of Muñjapṛṣṭha is a holy place celebrated in the three worlds, / named Kanakanandā, frequented by hosts of brahmin seers.

2.36.s:
tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti saśarīrā dvijātayaḥ /
dattaṃ cāpi sadā śrāddhamakṣayaṃ samudāhṛtam /
ṛṇaistribhirnaraḥ snātvā mucyate kṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ //
2.36.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा दिवं यान्ति सशरीरा द्विजातयः ।
दत्तं चापि सदा श्राद्धमक्षयं समुदाहृतम् ।
ऋणैस्त्रिभिर्नरः स्नात्वा मुच्यते क्षीणकल्मषः ॥
2.36.m: Having bathed there, twice-born men go bodily to heaven, / and an ancestral offering rite given there is declared to be forever imperishable. / Having bathed, a person is freed from the three debts, sins diminished.

2.36.s:
mānase sarasi snātvā śakrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet /
uttaraṃ mānasaṃ gatvā siddhiṃ prāpnotyanuttamām //
2.36.d:
मानसे सरसि स्नात्वा शक्रस्यार्धासनं लभेत् ।
उत्तरं मानसं गत्वा सिद्धिं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥
2.36.m: Having bathed in Lake Mānasa, one obtains half the seat of Śakra; / having gone to Northern Mānasa, one attains unsurpassed perfection.

2.36.s:
tasmānnirvartayecchrāddhaṃ yathāśakti yathābalam /
kāmān salabhate divyān mokṣopāyaṃ ca vindati //
2.36.d:
तस्मान्निर्वर्तयेच्छ्राद्धं यथाशक्ति यथाबलम् ।
कामान् सलभते दिव्यान् मोक्षोपायं च विन्दति ॥
2.36.m: Therefore, one should perform an ancestral offering rite according to one's capacity and strength; / one obtains divine desires and finds the means to liberation.

2.36.s:
parvato himavānnāma nānādhātuvibhūṣitaḥ /
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi so 'śītistvāyato giriḥ /
siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇo devarṣigaṇasevitaḥ //
2.36.d:
पर्वतो हिमवान्नाम नानाधातुविभूषितः ।
योजनानां सहस्राणि सो ऽशीतिस्त्वायतो गिरिः ।
सिद्धचारणसंकीर्णो देवर्षिगणसेवितः ॥
2.36.m: There is a mountain named Himavat, adorned with various minerals; / that mountain extends eighty thousand yojanas in length, / crowded with siddhas and cāraṇas, frequented by hosts of celestial seers.

2.36.s:
tatra puṣkariṇī ramyā suṣumnā nāma nāmataḥ /
tatra gatvā dvijo vidvān brahmahatyāṃ vimuñcati //
2.36.d:
तत्र पुष्करिणी रम्या सुषुम्ना नाम नामतः ।
तत्र गत्वा द्विजो विद्वान् ब्रह्महत्यां विमुञ्चति ॥
2.36.m: There is a lovely lotus pool there, Suṣumnā by name; / having gone there, a wise twice-born man is freed from the murder of a brahmin.

2.36.s:
śrāddhaṃ bhavati cākṣayyaṃ tatra dattaṃ mahodayam /
tārayecca pitṝn samyag daśa pūrvān daśāparān //
2.36.d:
श्राद्धं भवति चाक्षय्यं तत्र दत्तं महोदयम् ।
तारयेच्च पितॄन् सम्यग् दश पूर्वान् दशापरान् ॥
2.36.m: An ancestral offering rite given there brings great prosperity and becomes imperishable; / and one properly delivers ten previous and ten subsequent ancestors.

2.36.s:
sarvatra himavān puṇyo gaṅgā puṇyā samantataḥ /
nadyaḥ samudragāḥ puṇyāḥ samudraśca viśeṣataḥ //
2.36.d:
सर्वत्र हिमवान् पुण्यो गङ्गा पुण्या समन्ततः ।
नद्यः समुद्रगाः पुण्याः समुद्रश्च विशेषतः ॥
2.36.m: Himavat is holy everywhere; the Gaṅgā is holy on all sides; / the rivers flowing to the ocean are holy, and especially the ocean.

2.36.s:
badaryāśramamāsādya mucyate kalikalmaṣāt /
tatra nārāyaṇo devo nareṇāste sanātanaḥ //
2.36.d:
बदर्याश्रममासाद्य मुच्यते कलिकल्मषात् ।
तत्र नारायणो देवो नरेणास्ते सनातनः ॥
2.36.m: Having reached the hermitage of Badarī, one is freed from the taint of the Kali age; / there the eternal god Nārāyaṇa stays with Nara.

2.36.s:
akṣayaṃ tatra dānaṃ syāt japyaṃ vāpi tathāvidham /
mahādevapriyaṃ tīrthaṃ pāvanaṃ tad viśeṣataḥ /
tārayecca pitṝn sarvān dattvā śrāddhaṃ samāhitaḥ //
2.36.d:
अक्षयं तत्र दानं स्यात् जप्यं वापि तथाविधम् ।
महादेवप्रियं तीर्थं पावनं तद् विशेषतः ।
तारयेच्च पितॄन् सर्वान् दत्त्वा श्राद्धं समाहितः ॥
2.36.m: A gift made there becomes imperishable, as does what is to be muttered; / that holy place, dear to Mahādeva, is especially purifying; / having offered an ancestral offering rite with concentration, one delivers all ancestors.

2.36.s:
devadāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ siddhagandharvasevitam /
mahādevena devena tatra dattaṃ mahad varaṃ //
2.36.d:
देवदारुवनं पुण्यं सिद्धगन्धर्वसेवितम् ।
महादेवेन देवेन तत्र दत्तं महद् वरं ॥
2.36.m: The holy Devadāru forest is frequented by siddhas and gandharvas; / there a great boon was granted by the god Mahādeva.

2.36.s:
mohayitvā munīn sarvān punastaiḥ saṃprapūjitaḥ /
prasanno bhagavānīśo munīndrān prāha bhāvitān //
2.36.d:
मोहयित्वा मुनीन् सर्वान् पुनस्तैः संप्रपूजितः ।
प्रसन्नो भगवानीशो मुनीन्द्रान् प्राह भावितान् ॥
2.36.m: Having deluded all the sages, and then worshipped by them, / the gracious, blessed Lord spoke to the purified eminent sages:

2.36.s:
ihāśramavare ramye nivasiṣyatha sarvadā /
madbhāvanāsamāyuktāstataḥ siddhimavāpsyatha //
2.36.d:
इहाश्रमवरे रम्ये निवसिष्यथ सर्वदा ।
मद्भावनासमायुक्तास्ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यथ ॥
2.36.m: "You shall dwell forever here in this best, lovely hermitage; / endowed with meditation upon me, you will then attain perfection.

2.36.s:
ye 'tra māmarcayantīha loke dharmaparā janāḥ /
teṣāṃ dadāmi paramaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ hi śāśvatam //
2.36.d:
ये ऽत्र मामर्चयन्तीह लोके धर्मपरा जनाः ।
तेषां ददामि परमं गाणपत्यं हि शाश्वतम् ॥
2.36.m: "Those people devoted to righteousness who worship me here in this world, / to them I grant the supreme, eternal status of a Gaṇa leader.

2.36.s:
atra nityaṃ vasiṣyāmi saha nārāyaṇena ca /
prāṇāniha narastyaktvā na bhūyo janma vindati //
2.36.d:
अत्र नित्यं वसिष्यामि सह नारायणेन च ।
प्राणानिह नरस्त्यक्त्वा न भूयो जन्म विन्दति ॥
2.36.m: "I shall dwell here perpetually together with Nārāyaṇa; / abandoning life-breaths here, a human being does not find rebirth again.

2.36.s:
saṃsmaranti ca ye tīrthaṃ deśāntaragatā janāḥ /
teṣāṃ ca sarvapāpāni nāśayāmi dvijottamāḥ //
2.36.d:
संस्मरन्ति च ये तीर्थं देशान्तरगता जनाः ।
तेषां च सर्वपापानि नाशयामि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.36.m: "And those people who remember this holy place having gone to another land, / their sins too I destroy, O best of twice-born men.

2.36.s:
śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tapo homaḥ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tathā /
dhyānaṃ japaśca niyamaḥ sarvamatrākṣayaṃ kṛtam //
2.36.d:
श्राद्धं दानं तपो होमः पिण्डनिर्वपणं तथा ।
ध्यानं जपश्च नियमः सर्वमत्राक्षयं कृतम् ॥
2.36.m: "Ancestral offering rite, gift, asceticism, fire oblation, and likewise the offering of funeral balls, / meditation, recitation, and religious observances—all performed here is imperishable.

2.36.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena draṣṭavyaṃ hi dvijātibhiḥ /
devadāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ mahādevaniṣevitam //
2.36.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन द्रष्टव्यं हि द्विजातिभिः ।
देवदारुवनं पुण्यं महादेवनिषेवितम् ॥
2.36.m: "Therefore, by every effort, the holy Devadāru forest, / frequented by Mahādeva, should be seen by twice-born men.

2.36.s:
yatresvaro mahādevo viṣṇurvā puruṣottamaḥ /
tatra sannihitā gaṅgātīrthānyāyatanāni ca //
itī śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge ṣaṭtriśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.36.d:
यत्रेस्वरो महादेवो विष्णुर्वा पुरुषोत्तमः ।
तत्र सन्निहिता गङ्गातीर्थान्यायतनानि च ॥
इती श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे षट्त्रिशो ऽध्यायः
2.36.m:
"Where the Lord Mahādeva is, or Viṣṇu the Supreme Spirit, / there the Gaṅgā, holy places, and temples are present."

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the latter section of the Kūrma Purāṇa, in the compilation of six thousand [verses].
